rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's favor and mercy informed the Prophet through revelation and alerted him to the truth.
rows.anchor: بإعلامك بماهم عليه بالوحى وتنبيهك على الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view identifies God's favor as prophethood and His mercy as protection from error.
rows.anchor: وقيل : لولا فضله بالنبوة ورحمته بالعصمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view identifies the favor as prophethood and the mercy as revelation.
rows.anchor: وقيل : لولا فضله بالنبوة ورحمته بالوحى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation is God's safeguarding and protecting the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المراد لولا حفظه لك وحراسته إياك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The faction can mean Asir ibn Urwa and his associates among those who betrayed the trust.
rows.anchor: والمراد بهم أسير بن عروة وأصحابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another identification is those defending Tuʿma who knew the real facts of the case.
rows.anchor: أو الذابون عن طعمة المطلعون على كنه القصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun may refer to people generally, with the faction being those who supported the thief or dishonest trustee.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الضمير راجعا إلى الناس والمراد بالطائفة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that a Thaqif delegation sought a pledge not to break their idols and to worship al-ʿUzza for a year; the Prophet refused, God protected him, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أنهم قدموا على رسول الله

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim says the faction was hypocrites who plotted unsuccessfully to destroy the Prophet, whom God guarded.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي مسلم أنهم المنافقون هموا بما لم ينالوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They sought to divert the Prophet from judging justly.
rows.anchor: أي بأن يضلوك عن القضاء بالحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may mean diverting him from following the revelation about idols.
rows.anchor: أو عن اتباع ماجاءك فى أمر الأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may also mean to destroy him; the Qurʾan uses this sense in its question about being lost in the earth.
rows.anchor: أو بأن يهلكوك وقد جاء الإضلال بهذا المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although only their effect is explicitly negated, the wording denies their intention to signal that their effort had no effect at all.
rows.anchor: وانما نفى همهم مع أن المنفى إنما هو ثأثيره فقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading takes this as an effective plot, which in reality could not occur.
rows.anchor: وقيال المراد هو الهم المؤثر ولاريب فى انتفائه حقيقة

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says they were Muslims and did not intend to mislead the Prophet; they believed their action was right.
rows.anchor: وقال الراغب : إن القوم كانوا مسلمين ولم يهموا بإضلاله

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqa allows an omitted answer to the conditional, estimated as: without God's favor they would have misled you, followed by an independent clause.
rows.anchor: وجوز أبو البقاء أن يكون الجواب محذوفا والتقدير ولولا فضل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Abu al-Baqa's parsing, lahamma is an independent resumption meaning they certainly intended it.
rows.anchor: ثم استأنف بقوله سبحانه : لهمت أى لقد همت بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They only turn themselves from the truth, or destroy themselves as the consequences and harm return upon them.
rows.anchor: أى مايزيلون عن الحق إلا أنفسهم أو مايهلكون إلا إياها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement is parenthetical, and the following statement about harming the Prophet is coordinated with it.
rows.anchor: والجملة اعتراضية وقوله تعالى : ( ومايضرونك من شىء ( عطف عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its coordination with the preceding infinitive phrase is formal only; min is extra, making the phrase an accusative cognate object meaning no harm whatsoever.
rows.anchor: وعطفه على أن يضلوك وهم محض و من صلة والمجرور فى محل النصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God preserves the Prophet from error in judgment; any thought he had followed the apparent evidence and the speakers' assurances without knowing the hidden truth.
rows.anchor: لما أنه تعالى عاصمك عن الزيغ فى الحكم وأما ماخطر ببالك فكان عملا منك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God protects him from appeasing or following the views of heretics against revelation.
rows.anchor: أو لما أنه سبحانه عاصمك عن المداهنة والميل إلى آراء الملحدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation is that God promised to protect him from people and prevent them from reaching him.
rows.anchor: أو لما أنه جل شأنه وعدك العصمة من الناس وحجبهم عن التمكن منك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book and wisdom together refer to the Qurʾan, which combines both qualities.
rows.anchor: أى القرآن الجامع بين العنوانين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view identifies wisdom with the Sunna.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المراد بالحكمة السنة وقد تقدم الكلام فى تحقيق ذلك

rows.speaker: الأجهوري والطبرسي
rows.claim: Al-Ajhuri, with a similar indication from al-Tabarsi, reads the revelation as the reason for the preceding divine protection.
rows.anchor: على ما قال الاجهورى : فى موضع التعليل لما قبلها لما قبلها والى ذلك أشار الطبرسى

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim does not accept that the revelation clause explains the preceding protection clause.
rows.anchor: وهو غير مسلم على ماذهب اليه أبو مسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God taught him through kinds of revelation things he had not known, including hidden affairs, inward thoughts, and how to undo hostile schemes.
rows.anchor: وعلمك ( بأنواع الوحى ( مالم تكن تعلم ( أى الذى لم تكن تعلمه من خفيات الأمور

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas interprets the unknown matters as worldly affairs and legal rulings.
rows.anchor: أو من أمور الدنيا وأحكام الشرع كما روى عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak explains the knowledge as what is good and evil.
rows.anchor: أو من الخير والشر كما قال الضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is knowledge of reports about earlier and later peoples, or all the listed kinds of knowledge together.
rows.anchor: أو من أخبار الأولين والآخرين كما قيل أو من جميع ماذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some interpret the object of knowledge as the secrets of the Book and wisdom: God disclosed their mysteries and realities to him.
rows.anchor: ومن الناس من فسر الموصول بأسرار الكتاب والحكمة أى أنه سبحانه أنزل عليك ذلك

rows.speaker: البحر
rows.claim: Al-Bahr favors the inclusive sense of the knowledge rather than limiting it to one listed interpretation.
rows.anchor: فتكون الجملة الثانية كالتتمة للجملة الأولى واستظهر فى البحر العموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's favor exceeds expression and description; among its instances are universal prophethood, supreme leadership, and the greatest intercession on Resurrection Day.
rows.anchor: لاتحويه عبارة ولاتحيط به إشارة ومن ذلك النبوة العامة والرياسة التامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to recite is coordinated with an omitted clause connected to the preceding mention of Moses.
rows.anchor: عطف على مقدر تعلق به قوله تعالى : وإذ قال موسى الخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One coherence reading makes the story a prelude to Israel's later offenses, after laws were prescribed and messengers brought proofs.
rows.anchor: من حيث أنه تمهيد لما سيأتى إن شاء الله تعالى من جنايات بنى إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading contrasts cowardice about killing in the earlier episode with boldness in this killing, while both acts are sins.
rows.anchor: وقيل : من حيث أن فى الأول الجبن عن القتل وفى هذا الإقدام عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun most naturally refers to the Israelites; recitation informs them of obscure material in their scriptures, known to the Prophet only by revelation, establishing proof against them.
rows.anchor: وضمير عليهم يعود على بنى إسرائيل كما هو الظاهر إذ هم المحدث عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the pronoun as referring to Muhammad's community: recite the story to your people.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الضمير عائد على هذه الأمة أى اتل يا محمد على قومك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most exegetes identify the two sons as Habil and Qabil, sons of Adam himself.
rows.anchor: وكانا باجماع غالب المفسرين ابنى آدم عليه السلام لصلبه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says they were two men from the Children of Israel.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن : كانا رجلين من بنى إسرائيل

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud and other Companions relate that Adam's children were born as boy-girl twins and sibling groups intermarried by necessity; Qabil rejected Habil's request for his more beautiful twin, Aqleema, so Adam made marriage depend on whose offering God accepted.
rows.anchor: ماأخرجه ابن جرير عن ابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة
rows.claim: In the same report Adam entrusted the sons to the sky, earth, and mountains, all of which declined; Qabil accepted the trust while Adam went to Mecca.
rows.anchor: فقال آدم للسماء : احفظى ولدى بالأمانة فأبت وقال للأرض : فأبت

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة
rows.claim: Habil offered a ewe, or according to another version a ram; Qabil offered grain, ate its best kernel, and fire consumed Habil's offering as the sign of acceptance while leaving Qabil's untouched.
rows.anchor: فقرب هابيل جذعة وقيل : كبشا وقرب قابيل حزمة سنبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam ordered the test knowing Qabil's offering would not be accepted; he did not mean that acceptance would have made the disputed marriage permissible.
rows.anchor: وإنما أمر بذلك لعلمه أنه لايقبل من قابيل لا أنه لو قبل جاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bi-al-haqq may describe an omitted verbal noun, meaning a recitation characterized by truth and accuracy.
rows.anchor: متعلق بمحذوف وقع صفة لمصدر اتل أى اتل تلاوة متلبسة بالحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is a circumstantial phrase describing the reciter or the account, true and consistent with earlier scriptures.
rows.anchor: أو حال من فاعل اتل أو من مفعوله متلبسا أنت أو نبأهما بالحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idh is a time adverb attached to nabaa; although nabaa is originally a verbal noun, its verbal force permits the time phrase.
rows.anchor: ظرف لنبأ وعمل فيه لأنه مصدر فى الأصل والظرف يكفى فيه رائحة الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A proposed attachment as a circumstantial phrase from an omitted element is objected to because past idh does not fit the future recite; al-Alusi replies that the two parses differ.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون متعلقا بمحذوف وقع حالا منه ورد بأنه حينئذ

rows.speaker: البحر
rows.claim: Al-Bahr rejects treating idh as a substitute for nabaa with an omitted noun, since idh is added to time expressions, not nabaa; the response says both constructions are semantically and grammatically sound.
rows.anchor: ورده فى البحر بأن إذ لايضاف اليها إلا الزمان نحو يومئذ وحينئذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurban means anything offered to draw near to God, including a sacrifice or other gift; it is singular because it is originally a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: والقربان اسم لما يتقرب به إلى الله تعالى من ذبيحة أو غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accepted offering was Habil's.
rows.anchor: فتقبل من أحدهما ( وهو هابيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qabil's offering was rejected because he resented God's ruling that he could not marry his twin sister.
rows.anchor: لأنه سخط حكم الله تعالى وهو عدم جواز نكاح التوأمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speech clause resumes the narrative as an implicit question and answer: what did the one whose offering failed say?
rows.anchor: قال ( استئناف سؤال نشأ من الكلام السابق كأنه قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qabil's threat arose from envy at Habil's accepted offering and standing with God; another view attributes it to the prospect of losing the beautiful sister.
rows.anchor: لفرط الحسد على قبول قربانه ورفعة شأنه عند ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic final n is recited both geminated and, in a variant reading, lightened.
rows.anchor: بالنون المشددة وقرىء بالمخففة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reply means that God accepts offerings and worship only from the God-fearing, with sincerity directed to Him.
rows.anchor: إنما يتقبل الله ( أى القربان والطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqwa here means more than the first level of avoiding idolatry; Qabil's rejection resulted from his own abandonment of taqwa, not from Habil, so he should reform himself.
rows.anchor: وليس المراد من التقوى التقوى من الشرك التى هى أول المراتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a concise, wise reply that redirects blame to Qabil's own failure to acquire the taqwa that brings acceptance.
rows.anchor: إنك إنما أتيت من قبل نفسك لانسلاخها عن لباس التقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An envier should attribute deprivation to his own shortcomings and seek the qualities that brought another person favor, rather than trying to remove that person's blessing.
rows.anchor: أن الحاسد ينبغى أن يرى حرمانه من تقصيره ويجتهد فى تحصيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation takes Habil to mean that he will not evade God's threatened judgment, since the pious prefer obedience to life; al-Alusi calls this remote.
rows.anchor: وقيل : مراده الكناية عن أنه لايمتنع عن حكم الله تعالى بوعيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation says Habil will not kill Qabil in order to prevent being killed; the author also finds this reading remote.
rows.anchor: أو الكناية عن أنه لايقتله دفعا لقتله لأنه متق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse sternly rebukes people who perform deeds without the taqwa required for acceptance.
rows.anchor: وماأنعى هذه الآية على العاملين أعمالهم

rows.speaker: عامر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: At death, ʿAmir ibn ʿAbd Allah wept and explained that he heard God say acceptance is only from the God-fearing.
rows.anchor: وعن عامر بن عبد الله أنه بكى حين حضرته الوفاة

words: مَآ أَنَا۠ بِبَاسِطٍۢ يَدِىَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ
rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: One account says Habil was stronger but refrained from killing his brother out of fear of God and submitted, because resistance was forbidden under that law.
rows.anchor: قيل كان هابيل أقوى منه ولكن تحرج عن قتله واستسلم

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the Israelites had been commanded that a person whose life another sought must not resist until the attacker killed him or desisted.
rows.anchor: عن ابن جريج قال : كانت بنو إسرائيل قد كتب عليهم إذا الرجل بسط يده

words: مَآ أَنَا۠ بِبَاسِطٍۢ يَدِىَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ
rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: Another explanation is that Habil chose the greater reward of being killed rather than killing, assuming self-defense was allowed then.
rows.anchor: أو تحريا لما هو الأفضل الأكثر ثوابا وهو كونه مقتولا لا قاتلا

words: مَآ أَنَا۠ بِبَاسِطٍۢ يَدِىَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ
rows.speaker: الجصاص
rows.claim: Al-Jassas states that the sound legal position now obligates a person to prevent aggression against himself and others, even if doing so results in death.
rows.anchor: فالصحيح من المذهب أنه يلزم الرجل دفع الفساد عن نفسه وغيره

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and others understand Habil to mean that if Qabil initiates unjust aggression, Habil will not initiate aggression in return.
rows.anchor: ولذا قال ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما وغيره : إن المعنى فى الآية

words: مَآ أَنَا۠ بِبَاسِطٍۢ يَدِىَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Mujahid's and Ibn Jurayj's interpretation, the verse may be abrogated; whether that happened before the present religious law is disputed.
rows.anchor: وتكون الآية على ماقاله مجاهد وابن جريج : منسوخة وهل نسخت قبل شريعتنا

words: مَآ أَنَا۠ بِبَاسِطٍۢ يَدِىَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The obligation to oppose aggression is supported by the command to fight the party that transgresses until it returns, along with other verses and hadith.
rows.anchor: والدليل عليه قوله تعالى : فقاتلوا التى تبغى حتى تفىء وغيره من الآيات

words: مَآ أَنَا۠ بِبَاسِطٍۢ يَدِىَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another legal view says defense is not obligatory but is permissible.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنه لايلزم ذلك بل يجوز

words: مَآ أَنَا۠ بِبَاسِطٍۢ يَدِىَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ
rows.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet about civil strife says each step toward conflict is worse, and if it comes, one should be killed rather than become the killer; it supports avoiding such fighting.
rows.anchor: عن خباب بن الارت عنه ( صلى الله عليه وسلم ) أنه ذكر فتنة القاعد فيها خير

words: مَآ أَنَا۠ بِبَاسِطٍۢ يَدِىَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hadith that both the killer and killed Muslim are in Hell is understood to concern two people who each intended to kill the other, even if they did not fight.
rows.anchor: وأما من منع ذلك الآن مستدلا بحديث إذا التقى المسلمان بسيفيهما

rows.speaker: السيد المرتضى
rows.claim: Al-Sayyid al-Murtada says this is outside the dispute: the purpose-lam marks intended killing, which is blameworthy in every era, unlike defensive action aimed only at escape.
rows.anchor: وعن السيد المرتضى أن الآية ليست من محل النزاع لأن اللام الداخلة

words: مَآ أَنَا۠ بِبَاسِطٍۢ يَدِىَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic negation says Habil is not one to extend a hand against Qabil, repudiating even the preliminaries of killing rather than merely saying he would not kill.
rows.anchor: للمبالغة فى أنه ليس من شأنه ذلك ولا ممن يتصف به ولذلك أكد النفى

words: مَآ أَنَا۠ بِبَاسِطٍۢ يَدِىَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying he is not one to extend his hand, rather than simply saying he is not a killer, disavows the steps leading to murder.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل وما أنا بقاتل بل قال : بباسط للتبرى عن مقدمات القتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting the phrase toward me signals from the outset that the harm and consequences of aggression return to its perpetrator.
rows.anchor: وقدم الجار والمجرور المتعلق ببسطت إيذانا على ماقيل من أول الأمر برجوع ضرر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author also suggests that the fronting promptly reminds Qabil of himself and then of their brotherhood, which should prevent murder.
rows.anchor: ويحطر لى أنه قدم لتعجيل تذكيره بنفسه المنجر إلى تذكيره بالأخوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear of God explains Habil's refusal to raise his hand; it guides Qabil to fear God and implies that a killer does not fear Him.
rows.anchor: تعليل للامتناع عن بسط يده لقتله وفيه إرشاد قابيل إلى خشية الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fatawwaʿat means that his soul made the killing easy for him and widened its scope; the root can describe spacious pasture.
rows.anchor: فسهلته له ووسعته من طاع له المرتع إذا اتسع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Placing the soul's persuasion after Habil's speech reflects either a new act of resolve after resistance or Qabil's confidence once he saw Habil would not defend himself.
rows.anchor: لما أن بقاء الفعل بعد تقرر مايزيله وإن كان استمرارا عليه بحسب الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Habil his brother heightens the condemnation of what Qabil's soul urged him to do.
rows.anchor: والتصريح بأخوته لكمال تقبيح ماسولته نفسه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads faṭāwaʿat instead of the canonical faṭawwaʿat.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن فطاوعت وفيها وجهان : الأول أن فاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of al-Hasan's form treats Form III as equivalent to Form II, a usage also found by Sibawayh and others and close to the canonical reading.
rows.anchor: الأول أن فاعل بمعنى فعل كما ذكره سيبويه وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the reciprocal form is metaphorical: murder urges the soul, the soul resists, and in the end the soul yields to the stronger urge to kill.
rows.anchor: والثانى أن المفاعلة مجازية بجعل القتل يدعو النفس إلى الإقدام عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun li-hu adds emphasis and clarification, as in 94:1; the suggestion that it excludes someone else persuading him is unsound.
rows.anchor: للتأكيد والتبيين كما فى قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: مجاهد وابن جريج
rows.claim: A report says Qabil did not know how to kill; Iblis appeared as a bird and taught him by crushing another bird's head between two stones, after which Qabil killed his surrendered brother.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن جرير عن ابن مجاهد وابن جريج أن قابيل لم يدر كيف يقتل هابيل

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة
rows.claim: Another account says Qabil searched the mountains, then found Habil asleep while tending sheep and killed him with a rock, leaving the body exposed because he did not know how to bury it.
rows.anchor: وأخرج عن ابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة رضى الله تعالى عنهم أن قابيل طلب أخاه

rows.speaker: عمرو الشبعانى عن كعب الأخبار
rows.claim: Kaʿb al-Ahbar is reported by ʿAmr al-Shaʿbani to have located the killing on Mount Dayr al-Murran, with another report placing it on Mount Qasiyun.
rows.anchor: فعن عمرو الشبعانى عن كعب الأخبار أنه قتل على جبل دير المران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other locations given are near the pass of Hira or at Basra, where the great mosque stands.
rows.anchor: وقيل : عند عقبة حراء وقيل بالبصرة فى موضع المسجد الأعظم

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن فضالة
rows.claim: A report from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Fadala says God altered Qabil's mind and removed his heart after the murder, leaving him a wanderer until death.
rows.anchor: أخرج نعيم بن حماد عن عبد الرحمن بن فضالة أنه لما قتل قابيل هابيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An account says Qabil's formerly white body turned black after he killed Habil; Adam questioned him and attributed the change to his crime.
rows.anchor: وروى أنه لما قتله اسود جسده وكان أبيض فسأله آدم عن أخيه

rows.speaker: سالم بن أبي الجعد
rows.claim: Salim ibn Abi al-Jaʿd reports that Adam mourned his murdered son without laughing for a hundred years, then rejoiced when told he would have a son.
rows.anchor: عن سالم بن أبى الجعد قال : إن آدم عليه السلام لما قتل أحد بنيه

rows.speaker: محيى السنة
rows.claim: Muhyi al-Sunna says Seth was born fifty years after the murder, his name means God's gift and he replaced Habil; God taught him the hours and worship practices, sent him fifty scriptures, and made him Adam's heir.
rows.anchor: وذكر محيى السنة أنه عليه السلام ولد له بعد قتل ولده بخمسين سنة شيت

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir reports from Ali that Adam mourned Habil in verse; al-Khatib and Ibn ʿAsakir transmit a similar report from Ibn ʿAbbas, which became famous.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن على كرم الله تعالى وجهه قال : لما قتل ابن آدم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: ميمون بن مهران عن الحبر
rows.claim: Maimun ibn Mihran transmits Ibn ʿAbbas's denial that Adam composed poetry, since Muhammad and all prophets were equally forbidden to do so; he says Adam's Syriac elegy was later rearranged into Arabic verse by Yarub.
rows.anchor: وروى عن ميمون بن مهران عن الحبر رضى الله تعالى عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Arabic scholars found grammatical defects, imperfect rhyme, or forced poetic license in the attributed lines; the author says they should not even be attributed to Yarub because of their evident weakness.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعض علماء العربية إن فى ذلك الشعر لحنا أو إقواءا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qabil became a loser in this world and the next.
rows.anchor: دنيا وآخرة أخرج الشيخان وغيرهما عن ابن مسعود

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: The Prophet says that every unjustly killed person leaves a share of the bloodguilt on Adam's first son because he instituted murder.
rows.anchor: أخرج الشيخان وغيرهما عن ابن مسعود رضى الله تعالى عنه قال : قال رسول الله

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that the first killer shares Hell's punishment with its inhabitants and bears half their punishment.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمر رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال : إنا لنجد ابن آدم القاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited reports, including a report that Qabil was one of the wretched, indicate that he died an unbeliever.
rows.anchor: وهذا ونحوه صريح فى أن الرجل مات كافرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Qabil fled to Aden, where Iblis persuaded him to worship fire as the reason Habil's offering had been accepted; Qabil built a fire temple and became the first fire-worshipper.
rows.anchor: فأتاه إبليس عليهما اللعنة فقال : إنما أكلت النار قربان هابيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi says Qabil likely bears the burden of later fire-worship and perhaps of everyone who worships something other than God.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن عليه أيضا وزر من يعبد النار بل لايعبد أن يكون عليه وزر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asbaha does not prove the killing happened at night; Arabs use it for coming into a state of loss regardless of time.
rows.anchor: فان من عادة العرب أن يقولوا : أصبح فلان خسار الصفقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording became one of the losers, rather than simply a loser, intensifies the claim even though no one else had yet lost as he did.
rows.anchor: وإنما لم يقل سبحانه فأصبح خاسرا للمبالغة وإن لم يكن حينئذ

words: إِنَّمَا وَلِيُّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After prohibiting alliance with Jews and Christians and giving its reason, the verse identifies by restriction those truly entitled to the believers' allegiance.
rows.anchor: ثم إنه سبحانه لما قال : لاتتخذوا اليهود والنصارى أولياء وعلله بما علله ذكر عقب ذلك

words: إِنَّمَا وَلِيُّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast means those others ally with one another but are not your allies; reserve allegiance for God, the Messenger, and believers.
rows.anchor: لأن بعضهم أولياء بعض وليسوا بأوليائكم إنما أولياؤكم الله تعالى ورسوله

words: إِنَّمَا وَلِيُّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular wali despite multiple referents can show that God is the original ally, while the Messenger and believers are allies derivatively.
rows.anchor: وأفرد الولى مع تعدده ليفيد كما قيل : إن الولاية لله تعالى بالأصالة

words: إِنَّمَا وَلِيُّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parsing supplies an implied وكذلك before the Messenger and believers, preserving God as the grammatical original and the others as derivative allies; al-Alusi rejects treating the singular as simply a plural.
rows.anchor: فيكون التقدير إنما وليكم الله سبحانه وكذلك رسوله

words: إِنَّمَا وَلِيُّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative supplies a plural predicate for the full list; the separation emphasizes that the others become allies through God's appointment, so the two analyses converge in meaning.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يقال : التقدير إنما وليكم الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا أولياؤكم

words: إِنَّمَا وَلِيُّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Halabi's observation that wali can grammatically serve singular, dual, or plural does not explain the rhetorical reason for changing the wording.
rows.anchor: أن قول الحلبى ويحتمل وجها آخر وهو أن وليا زنة فعيل

words: إِنَّمَا وَلِيُّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restriction is compatible with the Messenger and believers having delegated allegiance because God alone is the original and true ally.
rows.anchor: لأن الحصر باعتبارأنه سبحانه الولى أصالة وحقيقة وولاية غيره إنما هى بالاسناد اليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description of believers may be appositional to the earlier relative pronoun, an adjective by treating it as a noun, or a nominative or accusative phrase of praise.
rows.anchor: بدل من الموصول الأول أو صفة له باعتبار إجرائه مجرى الأسماء

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Abd Allah's reading includes the conjunction waw before those who establish prayer.
rows.anchor: وفى قراءة عبد الله و الذين يقيمون الصلاة بالواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is a circumstantial clause for the subjects of both verbs, describing them as humble and lowly before God while praying and giving zakah.
rows.anchor: حال من فاعل الفعلين أى يعملون ماذكر من إقامة الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view attaches the circumstance only to giving zakah and takes rukuʿ as the prayer bow, showing eagerness and promptness in doing good.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو حال مخصوصة بايتاء الزكاة والركوع ركوع الصلاة

words: إِنَّمَا وَلِيُّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that Ibn Salam and fellow converts, shunned by their people and isolated from marriage and conversation, asked the Prophet for help; he declared God and the Messenger their allies, then observed Ali give a silver ring to a beggar while bowing and recited the verse.
rows.anchor: أخرج الحاكم وابن مردويه وغيرهما عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما باسناد متصل

rows.speaker: حسان
rows.claim: Hassan's poem praises Ali for giving zakah while bowing and says God revealed this special wilayah and recorded it in the scriptures.
rows.anchor: فانشأ حسان رضى الله تعالى عنه يقول

words: إِنَّمَا وَلِيُّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟
rows.speaker: الشيعة
rows.claim: The Shiʿa use the report to argue that the verse was unanimously revealed about Ali, that wali means one with general authority to dispose of affairs, and therefore proves his Imamate and excludes others.
rows.anchor: وا ستبدل الشيعة بها على إمامته كرم الله تعالى وجهه ووجه الاستدلال بها

words: إِنَّمَا وَلِيُّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In response to the singular referring to one person, grammarians allow plural wording for an eminent individual, magnifying the actor as a community and making the deed a model for every believer; Abraham is called a nation.
rows.anchor: فقد جاء فى غير ماموضع وذكر علماء العربية أنه يكون لفائدتين : تعظيم الفاعل

words: إِنَّمَا وَلِيُّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟
rows.speaker: أهل السنة
rows.claim: The first Sunni response is reductio: the same exclusive reading would disqualify Hasan, Husayn, and the later twelve Imams, harming the Shiʿi argument more than the Sunni position.
rows.anchor: الأول النقض بأن هذا الدليل كما يدل بزعمهم على نفى إمامة الأئمة المتقدمين

words: إِنَّمَا وَلِيُّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟
rows.speaker: أهل السنة
rows.claim: The restriction cannot be made relative to earlier leaders if it is to prove exclusive authority, and later Imams do not all share the stated qualities.
rows.anchor: ولايمكن أن يقال : الحصر إضافى بالنسبة إلى من تقدمه

words: إِنَّمَا وَلِيُّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟
rows.speaker: الشيعة
rows.claim: The Shiʿi reply limits the exclusive authority to Ali's own period as Imam, not the periods of Hasan, Husayn, and those after them.
rows.anchor: وإن أجابوا عن النقض بأن المراد حصر الولاية فى الأمير كرم الله تعالى وجهه فى بعض الأوقات

words: إِنَّمَا وَلِيُّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟
rows.speaker: أهل السنة
rows.claim: The Sunni response accepts that Ali had general authority during his own imamate, while denying that it held during the three caliphs before him or his successors afterward.
rows.anchor: فمرحبا بالوفاق إذ مذهبنا أيضا أن الولاية العامة كانت له وقت كونه إماما

words: إِنَّمَا وَلِيُّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟
rows.speaker: أهل السنة
rows.claim: An argument that subordination to earlier caliphs diminished Ali, unlike the later imamate of his descendants, changes the proof: it assumes that prior subordination is a defect and that a rightful ruler can never be deficient, neither of which follows from the verse.
rows.anchor: هذا فرار وانتقال إلى استدلال آخر ليس مفهوما من الآية إذ مبناه على مقدمتين

words: إِنَّمَا وَلِيُّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟
rows.speaker: أهل السنة
rows.claim: The subordination argument is also challenged by Hasan and Husayn under Ali's authority and by Ali under the Prophet's authority.
rows.anchor: على أن هذا الاستدلال منقوض بالسبطين زمن ولاية الأمير كرم الله تعالى وجهه

words: إِنَّمَا وَلِيُّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟
rows.speaker: محمد الباقر
rows.claim: A second Sunni response denies consensus about the occasion: al-Naqqash reports Muhammad al-Baqir as saying the verse concerned the Emigrants and Helpers, with Ali included among them.
rows.anchor: فقد اختلف علماء التفسير فى ذلك فروى أبو بكر النقاش صاحب التفسير المشهور عن محمد الباقر
